newsitem.title: USA: US Jewish, Arab groups urge return to Oslo accords.
newsitem.headline: US Jewish, Arab groups urge return to Oslo accords.

text.p: As President Bill Clinton met on Tuesday with Israeli and Palestinian leaders, U.S. Arab and Jewish groups urged the White House to send a strong signal to negotiators to return to the Middle East peace process.

"Handshakes are not enough," the leaders of four American groups said in a statement at a joint news conference. "The Oslo agreements (signed by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in a White House ceremony in 1993) should be implemented promptly, with full compliance."

The four groups -- the Arab-American Institute, the Palestinian American Congress, Project Nishma and Americans for Peace Now -- said Tuesday's meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestine President Yasser Arafat were a prime occasion to apply U.S. pressure to comply with the terms of peace accords reached in Oslo, Norway.
This pressure could be signalled by something as simple as a strongly worded White House statement or a phone call, the groups' leaders said.

Most of the leaders condemned Israel's decision to open a tourist tunnel near sacred sites in Jerusalem, which precipitated fatal violence in the last week, but Mark Rosenblum of the Zionist group Americans for Peace Now said the tunnel was a side issue and the central point was the peace agreement.
"There has to be light at the end of the tunnel, not tunnel at the end of the light," Rosenblum said.

James Zogby, president of the Arab-American Institute, noted that any action Clinton took in this case could have an impact on upcoming U.S. presidential elections, but Zogby said Clinton's involvement might help, not hurt, his chances at the polls.

The Arab and Jewish leaders were countered by a small pro-Israel demonstration outside the White House, where protesters carried signs reading "Mr. Clinton, stop pressuring Israel" and "Yasser Arafat, still a terrorist".
About a dozen picketers marched in a circle, chanting slogans including "No support for murderers, no support for terrorists" and "Arafat murdered American citizens."
